chapter: Style, peers and the 1963 New Orleans scene
title: Sharkey Bonano at the Hurricane club in 1945, and his recent illness
summary: Watts remembers the Hurricane, a gambling club on Frenchman Street, where Sharkey played, and they argue about the location.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And when I come back out to home in 45, Alfred, he was at the hurricane, I think on Frenchman. Hurricane. Hurricane. What was that club over there on Frenchman Street?
I wasn't here, man.
And it was all in tux. He had six pieces, but strictly gambling joint right in town on Frenchman.
By the river.
Yeah. No. By the river. Back then, no. I was on Turo. I was on Turo in, let's see, Claymore. By the Turo in between Johnson and Priya. I was living on Turo.
They got a bar in there now, Gail, tell me. Yeah, but two or three blocks down. On Priya.
Oh, yeah.
Some people stay by the house right there. Yeah. They got a bar right on that corner. They got everything in there.
Maybe so, but this was two or three blocks down on Frenchman. See, big, big, big club there, the Hurricane.
No.
And Sharky was playing in there.
I don't know where he's coming to.
You know where he is? Legionfield. Well, maybe so. Legionfield. Maybe so.

Legionfield between Durbin and Roman. Yeah. That's where, I remember that just as good. That's where it was on Legionfield. Yeah. Well, that's where Sharky was working. Because I used to walk up there and visit him some night. They had a police. Yeah. Used to be detailed. There used to be detailed at the economy hall. Uh-huh. And he told me how they had to knock down and drag out. Yeah. They closed up the joint, you know. Oh, yeah. Used to fight too much.
Yeah. Uh-huh.
A guy named Moirline. That's what Pogge said.
Uh-huh.
He said he wasn't no kid to them Moirline.
Well, I went there, man,
to talk about a beautiful place in town.

People informal. And here Sharky and this man in tux, man. Uh-huh. And just nothing but gambling tables. Long ball, gambling table. And now they'd be up at the ball. They'd be drinking a while. Now and then they played music. I never saw nobody on the ballroom floor, but the music was to draw the people, I guess, see. And now and then Sharky and Emma get up there. Come on, watch. Sit on the bandstand. I go up there and sit down and listen at him play a few numbers. And he was pretty ageable then, in 45. But I mean he could still blow.
Huh?
Blind?
Sharky? No, he's coming back now. He had something.
Diabetes. Oh, what?
Something, I forget. He was sick for a while, but he's coming back.
Oh, really? I heard he was going blind. Diabetes. Sure enough.
He had it, but no, he's playing this month.
Playing. Diabetes?
I think the 10th or something he's playing at the Royal Orleans.
Oh, yeah?
